competition: Build, Ship, Shape: Amazon Developer Hackathon
winning_archetypes: Time-constrained frontline users receive a specific next action before a consequential decision window closes.
Operators detect a meaningful exception in noisy activity and see which intervention it requires.
Educators and coaches identify a missed step from process evidence and deliver targeted help.
Reviewers uncover consequential changes across versions with inspectable supporting evidence.
Households and coordinators adapt plans to changing conditions while satisfying explicit constraints.
Developers locate a concrete failure or divergence and understand its downstream effect.
mechanism_families: Deterministic and temporal rules turn contextual inputs into explainable decisions and deadlines; supported by wn-001, wn-003 and wn-015.
Constraint optimization and dynamic routing adapt plans to resource limits and changing events; supported by wn-008 and wn-018.
Streaming changepoint and anomaly detection isolate actionable deviations; supported by wn-005 and wn-027.
Trace capture, classification and replay expose skipped steps and recurring friction; supported by wn-006.
Time-aligned visual comparison, semantic diff and AST-aware diff expose consequential changes; supported by wn-007, wn-012 and wn-021.
Context linking, requirement extraction and gap planning connect evidence to missing actions; supported by wn-013, wn-017 and wn-019.
Low-bandwidth interaction, offline synchronization and prioritized relays preserve utility under connectivity constraints; supported by wn-004 and wn-009.
Metadata-aware attribution and causal analysis explain why outcomes diverge; supported by wn-010 and wn-011.
Localized sensor fusion and stakeholder-aware clustering convert scattered observations into situated context; supported by wn-016 and wn-025.
demo_patterns: Complete one live input-to-outcome loop: show the user's input, the mechanism operating and the resulting actionable output.
Compare the same case before and after intervention using an observable outcome rather than an unsupported benefit claim.
Inject a controlled anomaly and show detection, explanation and response; label simulated inputs clearly.
Change one constraint mid-demo and show the plan adapting while preserving its stated requirements.
Reveal a missed step or consequential change through replay, highlighting or a side-by-side comparison.
Stress a relevant constraint such as lost connectivity and demonstrate the remaining usable workflow.
For this brief, fit one proof loop within three minutes and show it functioning on the selected track's accepted platform; Bee demonstrations must use actual Bee-origin data.
anti_patterns: Basic Fire TV players, streaming catalogs or remote-controlled games without a specific stakeholder outcome and a substantive mechanism.
Single-turn Alexa+ Q&A or thin API wrappers that stop before completing a useful workflow.
Bee notification relays or passive logs without evidence-linked decisions or follow-through.
Ring motion alerts or live views without contextual interpretation or an actionable workflow.
A single text-generation call or storage-only AWS integration presented as the main technical contribution.
Typo, formatting or README-only contributions presented as substantive Open Source work.
Transplanting a supplied winner's domain and workflow verbatim instead of adapting its underlying pattern.
Overbuilding cross-device orchestration or advanced models beyond the solo developer's approximately ten-hour budget.
Treating these differentiation risks as measured submission saturation; the supplied brief does not establish actual category frequency.
